name: Mitochondria
kicker: Double-membraned cell organelle · Breaks down food to make usable ATP
dates: Found in nearly every cell in the body
briefing: Mitochondria are bean-shaped organelles nicknamed the “powerhouse of the cell” because they break down digested food to make ATP, the fuel nearly every cell runs on. Folds in their inner membrane, called cristae, pack in extra surface area for this chemical machinery, and each one even carries its own small loop of DNA, passed down only from a person’s mother. Billions of years ago they were likely free-living bacteria that got swallowed by a larger cell and simply stayed.

tossups.p: It’s not the chloroplast, but the endosymbiotic theory holds that this organelle also began as a free-living bacterium that got engulfed by a larger cell billions of years ago. Hydrogen ions moving across a concentration gradient inside this organelle, a process called chemiosmosis, helps power the enzyme ATP synthase.
tossups.r: Folds in this organelle’s inner membrane, called cristae, increase the surface area available for its chemical reactions. For 10 points, name this organelle, nicknamed the “powerhouse of the cell,” that makes ATP for the rest of the cell to use.

tossups.p: Because a sperm cell’s copies of this organelle are destroyed after fertilization, its DNA is passed down only from a person’s mother; the most recent common maternal ancestor traced this way is nicknamed for this organelle and the Bible’s Eve. This organelle performs oxidative phosphorylation along its folded inner membrane.
tossups.r: The Krebs cycle takes place in this organelle’s innermost compartment, called the matrix. For 10 points, name this organelle that is commonly called the “powerhouse of the cell” because it manufactures ATP.

tossups.p: A group of diseases affecting this organelle causes muscle cells to show “ragged red” fibers under a microscope, including one called MERRF syndrome. Releasing the protein cytochrome c from this organelle is an early step that triggers a cell’s programmed death, called apoptosis.

tossups.p: A series of four protein complexes, numbered one through four, work together in this organelle to build up a chemiosmotic gradient that its own ATP synthase then uses to generate ATP. The Krebs cycle, which feeds that process, occurs in this organelle’s innermost matrix.

clues.t: Nicknamed the “powerhouse of the cell”
Makes most of a cell’s ATP, its usable chemical fuel
Hosts the second half of cellular respiration, finishing the breakdown of digested food
Wrapped in two membranes: a smooth outer one and a folded inner one
Found in nearly every cell in the human body, though the exact number varies by cell type
Its fluid-filled matrix is where the Krebs cycle takes place
Its folded inner membrane carries the electron transport chain
Inner membrane folds called cristae add extra surface area for chemical reactions
Carries its own small loop of DNA, inherited only from a person’s mother
Builds a hydrogen-ion gradient across its inner membrane in a process called chemiosmosis
Its innermost fluid-filled space is called the matrix
Finishes ATP production through a step called oxidative phosphorylation
Its inner membrane holds the enzyme ATP synthase, which assembles the final ATP
The endosymbiotic theory says it began as a free-living bacterium engulfed by a larger ancient cell
Real tossups often flag “it’s not the chloroplast” before describing this organelle, since both arose the same way
Diseases of this organelle, like MERRF syndrome, make muscle fibers look “ragged” and red under a microscope
Releasing its protein cytochrome c is an early step that triggers apoptosis, a cell’s programmed death
Brown fat cells use a protein called thermogenin inside this organelle to make body heat instead of ATP
Because its DNA passes only from mother to child, the most recent shared maternal ancestor of all humans is an “Eve” named for it
Four numbered protein complexes in its inner membrane carry out the electron transport chain
Its small maternal genome is labeled mtDNA, separate from the cell’s main DNA in the nucleus
Packed densely into busy cells like muscle and liver cells, but absent from mature red blood cells

trap.title: Mitochondria, or chloroplasts?
trap.body: Both organelles have double membranes, both likely began as engulfed bacteria under the endosymbiotic theory, and both carry their own small DNA loop — which is exactly why several real tossups interrupt themselves to say “it’s not the chloroplast, but…” before describing this organelle. The key difference is direction: one breaks food down for energy, the other builds food up from sunlight.
trap.fix: If the clues mention breaking down food, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain, or ATP as a final product, it’s mitochondria. If the clues mention capturing sunlight, chlorophyll, or building glucose, it’s chloroplasts instead — never answer “chloroplast” for a mitochondria question.
trap.line: Real answer line: Mitochondria (accept mitochondrion; reject chloroplast).
